title.narrative: Integrated Nutrition, Health, WASH and agriculture response to address malnutrition in Goro Dola woreda of East Borena zone, Oromia region.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project will deliver an integrated multi-sectoral response to acute malnutrition in East Borana’s Goro Dola woreda through nutrition, health, WASH, and agriculture interventions. It will restore nutrition screening, SAM/MAM treatment, and IYCF-E services. Health facilities will be strengthened through mobile outreach teams, vaccination campaigns, MISP services, surveillance and disease control, risk communication and community engagement, provision and last mile delivery of essential medicines and therapeutic foods. WASH activities will improve access to safe water and sanitation to reduce disease transmission. Agriculture and livelihoods support will include distribution of drought-tolerant seeds and fodder seeds plus farm tools to vulnerable households. It restocks vulnerable PLW households with dairy goats, rehabilitates pasture via fodder seeds and cash-for-work, and supports livestock treatment and vaccination through vouchers for host communities, and IDPs. Protection and inclusion will be prioritized by ensuring all supported facilities are safe and accessible for women, children, older adults, and persons with disabilities. Protection risk assessments will be conducted to identify and mitigate risks, including sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA). Safe spaces will be established for vulnerable groups, and partnerships with local women’s, youth, and disability organizations will ensure tailored responses. Feedback and complaints mechanisms will be made available and actively promoted. The project will be implemented by Action for Development (lead) and Plan International, with staff trained on protection, gender, disability inclusion, and accountability to affected people. Assistance will be delivered through both cash and in-kind modalities to maximize reach and impact. This integrated approach will reduce malnutrition and preventable disease, improve service access, strengthen food security, and uphold protection standards aligned with EHF 2025 priorities.ltbrgtThe total budget envelop for this project is $400,000. Out of this, 60%- which $ 240,000.00 allocated to AFD (lead partner, local NGO) and 40% $160,000.00 is allocated to Plan International. $ 245,317.03 is purely allocated to activities and 53,139.66 is for program staff cost. Thus, the budget allocated to program cost is $298,456.69 ($245,317.03+53,139.66) which means 75% of the total budget allocated to program cost. The cost per beneficiary is $ 16 (Total budget $400,000.00/24,769).lt/pgt
